stand: Yemen's government presses its counter-offensive toward Bab al-Mandeb and Taiz; Saudi Arabia's ambassador says the strait is cleared, which Houthis deny, saying they repelled an advance from Lahij. Houthi missiles killed three Saudis, including a pilot, at Riyadh airport on 8 October, prompting wider flight suspensions and EU no-fly advisories. UN envoy Hans Grundberg warned Yemen has slid into full-scale war and urged political talks at the Security Council, where Saudi Arabia and Yemen's government pressed for action. Pakistan says its forces in Riyadh remain strictly defensive.

Military/logistical vehicles destroyed or disabled (government claim)

Fighters killed across all fronts in one day

claims.text: Yemen's government, backed by Saudi Arabia, launched Operation Dawn of Yemen to retake all Houthi-held territory, including Sanaa.
claims.by: Says: Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi, Presidential Leadership Council. Denies: —

claims.text: Houthi forces cut the main supply road linking besieged Taiz to the government's interim capital, Aden, encircling the city.
claims.by: Says: Yemeni security and military sources, via AFP. Denies: —

claims.text: Government forces say they recaptured the Red Sea port city of Mocha from the Houthis.
claims.by: Says: Yemeni government/Saba news agency. Denies: Houthi deputy governor of Taiz, Fuad Sinan.

claims.text: The Yemeni government's claim to have reached Mocha was premature, according to Yemeni military officials on the ground and analysts; fighting is concentrated around Dhubab district.
claims.by: Says: Yemen's government. Denies/disputes: Yemeni military officials on the ground and analysts.

claims.text: Saudi-led coalition says it has secured "air protection" over Bab al-Mandeb and destroyed hundreds of Houthi targets.
claims.by: Says: coalition spokesperson Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki. Denies: —; Al Jazeera says it could not independently verify.

claims.text: Houthis say they struck Saudi Aramco oil sites in Riyadh and Khurais with missiles and drones, causing large fires.
claims.by: Says: Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree. Denies: no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia.

claims.text: Three people were wounded in attacks on Jazan and Najran airports near the Yemen border.
claims.by: Says: Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation. Denies: —

claims.text: The latest fighting in Yemen has killed 959 people and wounded 4,207, Yemen's Ministry of Health and Population says.
claims.by: Says: Yemen's Ministry of Health and Population, via WHO. Denies: —

claims.text: More than 201,000 (201,217) people have been displaced since the war resumed, nearly all since 1 September, with Ta'iz governorate hardest hit.
claims.by: Says: International Organization for Migration, Director General Amy Pope. Denies: —

claims.text: Turkiye's support to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca pact is mainly defensive and technical — military equipment, intelligence sharing and weapons systems — not combat deployment.
claims.by: Says: Turkish and Saudi officials, via Reuters. Denies: —

claims.text: Yemen's Defence Ministry says Mocha has fallen; Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree now says Houthi fighters retain full control of all their advances.
claims.by: Says: Yemen's Defence Ministry. Denies: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree.

claims.text: 516,157 of Yemen's acutely malnourished children under five have the severe form of the condition, almost a quarter of the total.
claims.by: Says: United Nations, via Al Jazeera.

claims.text: Government-aligned Homeland Shield Forces launched a large-scale operation to retake Houthi-held al-Waziiya, west of Taiz; Houthis say they repelled the advance.
claims.by: Says: Yemen's army media centre, citing a military source. Denies: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree.

claims.text: A Saudi airstrike killed six members of one family, including four children, in Hajjah governorate.
claims.by: Says: Houthi health ministry.

claims.text: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched towards Khamis Mushait.
claims.by: Says: coalition spokesperson Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki.

claims.text: The coalition destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform in Sanaa and a Saada storage facility holding 20 ballistic missiles.
claims.by: Says: Saudi-led coalition, via Saudi Press Agency.

claims.text: Pakistan's role reportedly goes beyond the reconnaissance support already acknowledged: it has flown military equipment to Aden and deployed troops inside Saudi Arabia to help defend its borders.
claims.by: Says: unnamed sources in Pakistan, via Reuters.

claims.text: Houthis attacked Aden International Airport with ballistic missiles and drones, forcing a flight from Cairo to divert to Jeddah.
claims.by: Says: Yemen's Ministry of Transport. Denies: —

claims.text: Houthis say they fired at a Saudi military supply convoy at Camp Badr near Aden airport; the government says its runway and passenger terminal were hit.
claims.by: Says: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree. Denies: Yemen's Transport Ministry, which says the runway and terminal were targeted.

claims.text: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched north of Riyadh.
claims.by: Says: Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki. Denies: —

claims.text: Houthis claim fresh strikes on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Abha airport and the Khamis Mushait air base.
claims.by: Says: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree. Denies: no immediate Saudi confirmation.

claims.text: WHO's immediate funding requirement for Yemen's health response has risen from $9 million to $31 million.
claims.by: Says: WHO Representative in Yemen, Dr Syed Jaffar Hussain. Denies: —

claims.text: Cholera cases in Yemen have tripled in three weeks, with cases detected in displacement camps.
claims.by: Says: World Health Organization. Denies: —

claims.text: Saudi authorities confirmed three Saudi nationals, including Saudia pilot Capt Hamoud Ali Alkalthami, were killed in two Houthi attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid airport on 8 October — updating earlier reports of no immediate Saudi confirmation.
claims.by: Says: Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation; Saudia.

claims.text: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed 82 Houthi military targets, including 11 mountain-based missile storage sites in Saada, in retaliation for the airport attacks.
claims.by: Says: Saudi-led coalition spokesperson.

claims.text: Yemeni government forces say they have "neutralised" 1,860 Houthi fighters via 2,103 targeting operations since the counter-offensive began.
claims.by: Says: spokesperson for Yemen's army.

claims.text: The Institute for the Study of War said it was revising its assessment that Houthi coastal forces were collapsing, after evidence Houthi forces halted government-aligned advances.
claims.by: Says: Institute for the Study of War, via the Guardian.

claims.text: Independent observers said the Houthis were on course to capture Taiz, with signs government-aligned forces were pulling back to secure Aden.
claims.by: Says: unnamed independent observers, via the Guardian.

claims.text: A Houthi missile hit Taiz, a government-held city, wounding five civilians.
claims.by: Says: Yemen's Saba news agency, via AFP.

claims.text: Pakistani retired Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood was appointed first secretary-general of the Mecca pact alliance for a three-year term.
claims.by: Says: joint statement of Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye.

claims.text: Turkiye's parliament has not yet ratified the Mecca pact; ratification is expected within days, after which support could increase.
claims.by: Says: Omer Celik, spokesman for Turkish President Erdogan's AK Party.

claims.text: Houthis say they struck Riyadh airport with a ballistic missile; shrapnel from the strike or an interception left a parked Saudia Airlines plane destroyed by fire, with no passengers believed aboard.
claims.by: Says: Houthi military statement; sources briefed on the matter, via Reuters. Denies: Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment.

claims.text: The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted two ballistic missiles heading for Riyadh and one toward Khamis Mushait on 8 October.
claims.by: Says: coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki.

claims.text: Debris from an intercepted missile caused material damage to a kindergarten and medical clinic complex in Riyadh.
claims.by: Says: Saudi civil defence agency.

claims.text: Houthis warned airlines to avoid Saudi airspace entirely, except over Mecca and Medina, and threatened to target energy plants.
claims.by: Says: Houthi military statement.

claims.text: 131 flights to and from Riyadh had been cancelled by Friday afternoon, after hundreds of cancellations the day before — a larger toll than the earlier count of nearly half Thursday's departures — as Lufthansa, three Indian airlines and Etihad suspended or cancelled Riyadh services.
claims.by: Says: Flightradar24 data, via Reuters; Lufthansa, Etihad.

claims.text: Syria is weighing deploying troops to help Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, either defensively or in an offensive role.
claims.by: Says: one US and one Syrian defence official, via Reuters.

claims.text: Syria's foreign ministry says it stands firmly with Saudi Arabia but that its own focus is on domestic recovery, stopping short of confirming deployment.
claims.by: Says: Syrian foreign ministry diplomat, via Reuters.

claims.text: At least 3,700 refugees have crossed from Yemen into Djibouti since 10 September; UNHCR is preparing to assist another 10,000 who have not yet crossed.
claims.by: Says: UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR).

claims.text: Shipping insurance and reinsurance costs for vessels on the Red Sea route have nearly doubled, pushing some ships away from the Suez Canal and Red Sea.
claims.by: Says: Alessandra Roccasalvo, UNDP Djibouti representative.

claims.text: Saudi Arabia's ambassador to Yemen says allied forces have fully cleared the Bab al-Mandeb strait of Houthi fighters; a Houthi spokesperson denies this, saying an advance from Lahij was repelled.
claims.by: Says: Saudi ambassador to Yemen Mohammad Al-Jaber. Denies: Houthi spokesperson Ameen Hayyan.

claims.text: Houthis say they repelled a Saudi-backed advance from Lahij toward Bab al-Mandeb, destroying more than 22 armoured vehicles and killing or wounding dozens, including commanders.
claims.by: Says: Houthi spokesperson Ameen Hayyan.

claims.text: A Yemeni military source on the ground said fighting around Bab al-Mandeb remained fierce with limited advances, and that Houthi forces still held nearby Mocha, contradicting the Saudi ambassador's "cleared" claim.
claims.by: Says: unnamed Yemeni military source, via Reuters.

claims.text: The UN Special Envoy to Yemen told the Security Council the country has slid back into full-scale war and urged political talks rather than reliance on battlefield gains.
claims.by: Says: UN Special Envoy to Yemen Hans Grundberg.

claims.text: At least 46 civilians have been killed and more than 130 injured in Yemen since August, with children bearing a disproportionate toll, the UN says.
claims.by: Says: United Nations, via UN Special Envoy's briefing.

claims.text: Saudi Arabia and Yemen's government asked the UN Security Council to act against the Houthis, including reducing the flow of funding, weapons and technology to the group.
claims.by: Says: Saudi UN envoy Abdulaziz al-Wasil; Yemen's UN envoy Abdullah Ali Fadhel al-Saadi.

claims.text: France and Saudi Arabia are exploring ways for the French military to help protect the Yanbu oil terminal on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast.
claims.by: Says: unnamed sources, via Reuters.

claims.text: A Houthi military spokesman suggested flights into or out of Riyadh airport, including humanitarian flights, will need authorisation from a Houthi coordinating body in Sanaa.
claims.by: Says: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree.

claims.text: EU aviation regulator EASA widened its advisory against flying in Saudi airspace to cover an area in the northwest, and flight-risk body OPSGROUP told members to avoid Saudi Arabia entirely, after the Riyadh airport attacks.
claims.by: Says: European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA); OPSGROUP.

claims.text: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed three Houthi missile launch platforms and vowed a firm response to further attacks on civilians.
claims.by: Says: Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Maj Gen Turki al-Malki.

claims.text: Across Yemen overall, more than 22 million people need humanitarian support and about 5.2 million are displaced, UNHCR says, on top of the 200,000-plus newly displaced by the past month's fighting.
claims.by: Says: UNHCR, via ReliefWeb/MSF.

timeline.text: At least 3,700 refugees cross from Yemen into Djibouti since 10 September; UNHCR prepares to assist 10,000 more.
President Rashad al-Alimi announces in a televised address the start of Operation Dawn of Yemen to retake all Houthi-held territory.
Houthi fighters cut the main road linking Taiz to Aden, taking the al-Safiya area and its police station, encircling Taiz.
Houthis fire missiles and drones at Aramco sites in Riyadh and Khurais, claiming large fires; Saudi Arabia does not immediately confirm.
Government forces say they retook Dhubab district, its airport and the port city of Mocha; Houthis deny Mocha fell.
Saudi-led coalition launches an air campaign with 100 fighter jets, saying it has secured air protection over Bab al-Mandeb.
Government forces announce a strategic offensive on the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa.
Houthi fighters capture the town of Turbah in southwestern Yemen, advancing toward Taiz.
Saudi civil aviation authority says three people were wounded in attacks on Jazan and Najran airports near the Yemen border.
Defence ministers of Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia meet in Riyadh and agree to activate deterrence measures under their mutual defence pact.
Pakistan's defence minister says Pakistani forces are already providing reconnaissance support in Saudi Arabia; combat remains Saudi-led.
Pakistan's retired Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood is named first secretary-general of the Mecca pact alliance for a three-year term.
Yemen's Defence Ministry says Mocha has fallen; a Houthi military spokesman denies any retreat, calling reports "fabricated heroics".
Government and allied Popular Resistance Forces say they took the al-Manzara, al-Ashari and Dhiban mountains in Haifan, south of Taiz.
WHO says the fighting has killed at least 959 people and wounded 4,200+; IOM says over 184,000 have been displaced since the war resumed.
Houthis claim fresh strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid airport, the Rabigh Aramco refinery, Abha airport and the Khamis Mushait base; Riyadh does not confirm.
Government-aligned Homeland Shield Forces launch a large-scale operation to retake Houthi-held al-Waziiya, west of Taiz; Houthis say they repelled it.
Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Khamis Mushait.
Coalition says it destroyed a missile launch platform in Sanaa and a Saada depot holding 20 ballistic missiles.
Houthi health ministry says a Saudi strike killed six members of a family, four of them children, in Hajjah.
AFP sources on both sides say fighting across Yemen killed more than 270 government troops and Houthi fighters in a single day.
WHO warns of a critical funding gap for Yemen's health response as needs rise and trauma points go unstaffed.
Houthis attack Aden International Airport with ballistic missiles and drones; a flight from Cairo is diverted to Jeddah and the terminal evacuated.
Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched north of Riyadh.
Houthis claim fresh strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid airport, Abha airport and the Khamis Mushait air base; Riyadh does not confirm.
IOM says Yemen displacement has passed 200,000, reaching 201,217, with Ta'iz governorate hardest hit.
Turkiye says its support to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca pact is mainly defensive and technical, not combat deployment.
Yemeni military officials and analysts say the government's claim of reaching Mocha was premature; fighting is concentrated in Dhubab district.
Saudi civil aviation authority says Houthi attacks on Abha and King Khalid (Riyadh) airports killed three people and wounded 36.
Saudi-led coalition destroys 82 Houthi targets, including 11 missile storage sites in Saada, and vows the airport attacks "will not go unpunished".
A Houthi missile hits Taiz, wounding five civilians in a crowded street, Saba/AFP report.

ISW revises its view that Houthi coastal forces were collapsing, citing evidence Houthis halted government-aligned advances; observers see Houthis nearing Taiz and government forces pulling back toward Aden.
Southern Giants Forces, a pro-government militia, lead the push on Bab al-Mandeb and are positioned in the military airport sector of Dhubab district.
Houthi leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi marks the Hamas attack anniversary, accusing Saudi Arabia of undermining the Palestinian cause and criticising Al Jazeera's coverage.
Yemeni government forces claim to have "neutralised" 1,860 Houthi fighters since the counter-offensive began.
Houthis claim a missile strike on Riyadh airport; a parked Saudia Airlines plane is destroyed by fire, with no passengers believed aboard.
Coalition says it intercepted two missiles toward Riyadh and one toward Khamis Mushait.
Debris from an intercepted missile hits a kindergarten and medical clinic complex in Riyadh.
Houthis warn airlines off Saudi airspace except over Mecca and Medina, threatening to strike energy plants.
Lufthansa and Air India suspend flights to Riyadh; nearly half of Thursday's departures from Riyadh airport are cancelled.
Qatar, Oman and Egypt condemn the Houthi attacks on Saudi airports.
Reuters reports Syria is weighing a troop deployment to help Saudi Arabia; Syria's foreign ministry says its focus remains domestic.
Reports say Pakistan has flown military equipment to Aden and deployed troops in Saudi Arabia to help defend its borders.
Saudi civil aviation authority confirms three Saudi nationals, including a Saudia pilot, were killed in Thursday's attacks on Riyadh airport.
Saudi ambassador to Yemen claims Bab al-Mandeb is cleared of Houthi forces; Houthi spokesperson Ameen Hayyan denies it, saying an advance from Lahij was repelled.
UN Special Envoy Hans Grundberg tells the Security Council Yemen has slid back into full-scale war and urges political talks.
EASA widens its no-fly advisory for Saudi airspace and OPSGROUP tells members to avoid Saudi Arabia entirely after the Riyadh airport attacks.
Houthis sweep down Yemen's Red Sea coast, seizing about 150km of coastline and areas around Bab al-Mandeb.
Houthi rebels capture Yemen's Perim Island, the narrowest point of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
